headline: Colorado's Wildlife Bridge Cuts Highway Deaths by 91 Percent

summary_short: A 209-by-200-foot wildlife overpass near Larkspur, Colorado has cut deer collisions on I-25 by 91 percent in just nine months, restoring migration routes for elk and pro…
body:
Nine months after opening, North America's largest wildlife overpass has transformed a deadly stretch of Interstate 25 in Colorado. The 209-by-200-foot structure near the Greenland exit between Larkspur and Monument has cut vehicle collisions by 91 percent—a dramatic reversal of conditions that once claimed roughly one deer per day during peak migration seasons. The project, which finished ahead of schedule and under budget at $15 million, represents a rare convergence of wildlife science and infrastructure planning that is now paying measurable dividends.

For decades, I-25 functioned as an impassable barrier across seasonal migration corridors. Pronghorn traveling between Trinidad and Greenland had no safe passage; elk herds faced the same impossible choice. Within weeks of the December opening, camera footage captured elk herds crossing together and pronghorn appearing on the western side of I-25 for the first time in decades. One image showed an elk cow guiding her calf safely underneath the highway—a moment that crystallized six years of collaborative effort.

What makes this project especially noteworthy is its comprehensive approach. Beyond serving large game animals, wildlife managers constructed covered wood corridors on the overpass surface to shelter smaller creatures: the federally threatened Preble's meadow jumping mouse, northern leopard frogs, reptiles, and amphibians now use the crossing safely. The economics work too. CDOT estimates wildlife crossings typically pay for themselves within 15 years through prevented accidents and property damage. With a recently passed state law expected to generate $3 million annually for wildlife mitigation, Colorado has identified seven additional priority corridors—from Raton Pass to areas near Fort Collins and Boulder—ready for similar treatment. Success, it turns out, requires more than engineering. It demands what one CDOT manager called the essential ingredient: "everybody marching in the same direction."
quick_facts: 209-by-200-foot overpass opened December near Larkspur, Colorado
Collisions reduced 91 percent in first nine months
Cost $15 million, finished under budget with federal and state funds
Pronghorn now crossing I-25 west for first time in decades
State law generates $3 million annually for future wildlife crossings
